LINE ITEM

Peak load contribution tag

FIG. 01 — SCHEMATIC

Visual representation of Peak load contribution tag mechanics.

The Short Answer: Peak load contribution tag is in some markets a customer's draw during a small number of system peak hours sets an obligation that shapes charges for a later year. On a commercial bill, this line typically indicates shave peak exposure.

FIG. 02 — STRUCTURAL CONTEXT

Why Utilities Use This Model

Utilities impose this specific charge to recover the capital and operational costs of maintaining grid reliability. For shave peak scenarios, this ensures the infrastructure can handle sudden spikes in demand without causing localized brownouts or requiring expensive emergency power purchases.

🧮 Worked Scenario

If your facility has a peak demand of 50kW and your tariff charges $10/kW (typical for a RATCHET band), that single line item costs you $500/month, regardless of how many kWh you actually use.

FIG. 03 — COMMON ERRORS

The Common Misread

The most common mistake is assuming the charge is treated as current-month behaviour when it reflects a past event. In reality, the billing structure separates these mechanics to reflect grid realities.

How to spot this: Look on page 2 or 3 of your PDF bill under sections labeled "Detailed Charges," "Tariff Schedule," or "Riders." It may appear abbreviated (e.g., "Dem Chg" or "Fac Chg").

🎯 Your One Action This Week

Focus on shave peak. Review your last two bills to see if this specific lever is driving your costs.
